  \(F\), there are nonnegative ordinary smooth \(\theta_i\), each
  compactly supported inside \(U_i\), with \(\sum_i\theta_i=1\)
  near \(F\). This follows from CLD Corollary 15.2.5 and smooth
  functional calculus. For each \(x\in F\), take a smooth bump
  equal to one near \(x\) with compact support in a cover member.
  Smooth nonnegative composition preserves these properties.
  Compactness gives finitely many such bumps; group them by cover
  index as \(\psi_i\) and put \(s=\sum_i\psi_i\). Then \(s>0\)
  near \(F\). Take a further nonnegative smooth cutoff \(\chi\),
  equal to one near \(F\), with compact support in \(\{s>0\}\).
  Set \(\theta_i=\chi\psi_i/s\) there and extend by zero.
  Smoothness follows from compact support inside that open; the
  supports lie compactly inside their respective \(U_i\), and
  their sum is \(\chi\). Only this compact specialization is used;
  no general countable-at-infinity fixed-cover-index compact-support
  assertion is needed.
